findings.title: Flexing .small-action breaks its float-based right-aligned button
findings.body: Adding flexbox to .small-action makes its direct children flex items, so the existing float declarations on .topic-avatar and button are ignored. The button that previously used float:right will no longer be positioned at the right edge; without flex-grow on .small-action-desc, justify-content spacing, or margin-left:auto on the button, it will render immediately after the description text. This is likely a visual regression wherever small-action buttons appear.

findings.title: align-items mixin passes standard values to prefixed properties unchanged
findings.body: The mixin forwards $alignment directly to legacy prefixed properties such as -webkit-box-align and -ms-flex-align. Standard align-items values like flex-start and flex-end are not valid for those legacy syntaxes, which expect start/end. Current call sites only use center and baseline, but this reusable mixin will silently produce incorrect alignment for common future uses unless values are mapped.

findings.title: align-items mixin emits invalid -ms-align-items property
findings.body: The mixin outputs -ms-align-items, which is not a recognized Microsoft flexbox property. IE10/old Edge used -ms-flex-align, which is already emitted on the previous line. The invalid declaration only adds dead CSS and can confuse linting or debugging, so it should be removed.

findings.title: order mixin uses legacy ordinal-group values incorrectly
findings.body: The order mixin emits the same numeric value for standard order and legacy -webkit-box-ordinal-group / -moz-box-ordinal-group. The old ordinal-group property is 1-based, while standard order is 0-based, so order(0) or mixed positive/negative ordering can behave inconsistently or invalidly in legacy browsers. The legacy value should be adjusted, typically $val + 1, or the legacy declarations should be omitted unless specifically required.
